content.text: No MFN-type obligation exists anywhere in the Agreement. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
input.rationale: We reviewed every pricing and commercial location (§ 11 Fees, § 10 Maintenance and Support and its fee-bearing repair provisions, § 20 General Matters, and the definitions/Schedules list) and searched for parity, "no less favourable", best-price, right-to-match and third-party-offer language. The Agreement contains no most-favoured-nation or pricing-parity mechanic at all: Sparkling's only pricing obligation is to pay the fees set out in the Fee Schedule, and Garman's charging rights are limited to Fee Schedule rates for specified excluded repair causes. There is therefore no MFN obligation on Customer benefiting Garman, which meets our preferred position, so no redline is required. Note that we likewise have no MFN in our favour, which is permissible under this rule (a Customer-favourable MFN would be welcome but is not required).
